selection_noise_band.note: Approximate — computed from target mean variance across fold validation windows; proper noise band requires baseline skill MAE estimation per fold
selection_noise_band.h1: ~25-30 MAE (estimated; folds 1-2 val window is autumn quarter, fold 3 is autumn/winter of COVID year)
selection_noise_band.h90: unreliable from fold 3 alone (5 scoreable rows); use folds 1+2+3 pooled for h90 selection; formal estimate deferred to baseline skill

split_info.holdout_representativeness: The 2021+ holdout is FULLY post-regime (Mondays open) — training fold 3 now includes 30 post-regime rows (vs 0 in run_20260904T140437Z), which is a material improvement. However, 30 rows of post-regime training signal is still limited (~4-5 Mondays). The fold 3 validation window (Sep-Dec 2020, 95 rows) is entirely post-regime and provides the best available proxy for holdout performance, but: (1) COVID behavioral changes persisted into autumn 2020; (2) Gentse Feesten was cancelled in 2020 while holdout years (2021+) may resume it; (3) the -28.7% long-term demand trend continues beyond 2020. All model metrics are validation-only and optimistic by an unknown margin.

regime_coverage.note: This is the minimum viable post-regime representation in training. The prior run (run_20260904T140437Z) had 0 post-regime in training, which caused +8.5 MAE error on Mondays. 30 training rows vs 0 is a critical fix.

reasoning.deployment_simulation: Forecasting bread demand for future days (h=1 to 90 days ahead) from an origin date in recent history. The model is trained on historical patterns and evaluated on its ability to predict demands it has not seen.
reasoning.val_fairness: Fold 3 validation (Sep-Dec 2020, 95 rows post-regime) is the best available proxy for the 2021+ holdout. It captures the post-regime Monday pattern, COVID recovery demand levels, and winter seasonality. It does NOT capture the full Gentse Feesten pattern (2020 was cancelled) or the steady demand decline continuing into 2021+.
reasoning.regime_boundary: The fold 3 train cutoff (2020-06-30) falls exactly within the post-regime period — train includes only 30 days post-regime change. This is a deliberate choice: (1) ensures post-regime Monday pattern is in training, fixing the key error from the prior run; (2) leaves the full September-December post-regime window available for evaluation. Alternative of cutting at 2019-12-31 would be cleaner but repeats the prior run's 0%-post-regime error.
reasoning.alternative_considered: Cutting at 2019-12-31 (clean year boundary) would give 240 validation rows but 0 post-regime in training — same error as run_20260904T140437Z. Rejected in favour of 30 post-regime training rows.
reasoning.h90_constraint: The h=90 horizon has only 5 scoreable validation rows in fold 3. This makes per-horizon model selection for h=90 unreliable on fold 3 alone. Training MUST use all 3 folds when evaluating h=90 candidates. This is flagged as a constraint for Training and Diagnosis.

missing_handling.reasoning: Precipitation is highly seasonal in Belgium; month-median preserves seasonal pattern better than global median.

outlier_handling.reasoning: Extreme precipitation events are genuine signal — heavy rain affects foot traffic

missing_handling.source_mechanism: MCAR — rows with NULL are dates outside the competitor data coverage window (2017-07-01 to 2020-09-15) OR dates when no competitor was on holiday. The absence of a row means zero closures, not an unknown value.
missing_handling.reasoning: VerlofConcurrent.csv records events (competitor holidays). A missing row means the event did not occur. Filling with 0 is the correct value, not imputation. The comp_data_available indicator separates 'known zero' (within coverage, no holidays) from 'unknown' (outside coverage window).

agent_initiated_findings.title: Weather parquet stores daily totals/extremes repeated for each hourly row — must use mean/max/min, NOT sum for aggregation
agent_initiated_findings.findings: Initial aggregation with 'sum' for Precipitation produced mean=29.9mm/day (13x Belgium annual average). Cross-run comparison with run_20260904T140437Z (mean=2.68) confirmed the parquet stores the daily total in each hourly row (Visual Crossing API format). Correct aggregation: mean(daily_total_repeated) = daily total. Precipitation mean after fix: 1.246mm/day.
agent_initiated_findings.reasoning: This is a common pitfall with Visual Crossing hourly weather exports. Summing 24 copies of the daily total produces wildly inflated values. The same issue applies to Snow_depth and Wind_Gust (daily max repeated per hour — use max not sum).
agent_initiated_findings.recommendation: Feature Engineering scripts that use wx_Precipitation must NOT re-aggregate from raw parquet — use the pre-aggregated values from data/iteration_003_preprocess.csv.

agent_initiated_findings.title: VerlofConcurrent.csv uses ';' separator, not ','
agent_initiated_findings.method: error investigation when pandas read as 1-column frame
agent_initiated_findings.findings: Initial pd.read_csv with sep=',' produced a 2357×1 dataframe (all data in single column). Correct separator is ';'. After fixing: 2357×10 correctly parsed with date, winkel, verlof_concurrent_1-5, Highsales, lowsales, Actie columns.
agent_initiated_findings.reasoning: European CSV convention often uses semicolons when commas appear in values (e.g., Dutch number formatting). This is a consistent parsing requirement across runs.
agent_initiated_findings.recommendation: All downstream scripts that read VerlofConcurrent.csv must use sep=';', encoding='latin-1'.

agent_initiated_findings.title: h=90 horizon has only 5 scoreable validation rows in fold 3
agent_initiated_findings.method: count of val rows with date <= dataset_end - 90 days
agent_initiated_findings.findings: The fold 3 val window (2020-09-28 to 2020-12-31) has 95 rows total. For h=90, a val origin at date D requires a target at D+90 within the dataset. Dataset ends 2020-12-31, so last usable h=90 origin is approximately 2020-10-02. Only 5 val rows have origins ≤ 2020-10-02.
agent_initiated_findings.reasoning: This is a structural constraint of the dataset ending at 2020-12-31. With 5 scoreable rows, h=90 MAE estimation in fold 3 has very high variance. Training must pool all 3 folds for h=90 model selection.
agent_initiated_findings.recommendation: Training skill: use all 3 folds when scoring h=90 candidates. A h=90 result that appears to win in fold 3 alone (5 rows) is likely noise. Diagnosis should flag h=90 model selection as statistically uncertain until confirmed across all folds.

agent_initiated_findings.title: Fold 3 has only 30 post-regime training rows (June 1-30, 2020)
agent_initiated_findings.method: count of train rows with date >= 2020-06-01
agent_initiated_findings.findings: Fold 3 training (through 2020-06-30) includes only 30 post-regime rows. This gives approximately 4-5 Monday observations, which is the entire training signal for the regime_x_monday feature.
agent_initiated_findings.reasoning: 30 post-regime rows is dramatically better than 0 (prior run's error), but still limited. The model must learn Monday-level demand from ~4-5 data points. Feature Engineering should use the full post-regime DOW mean (from all 95 val rows) to set a reasonable prior for the Monday feature.
agent_initiated_findings.recommendation: Feature Engineering: regime_x_monday feature should not be shrunk or regularised aggressively — it has only 4-5 training examples and needs to learn from a small signal. Diagnosis: specifically check whether Monday val rows are systematically over- or under-predicted.

clarification_needed.question: wx_Precipitation mean=1.246mm/day post-imputation vs prior run's mean=2.68mm/day. Is this difference due to the imputation approach for 2010-2014 pulling the overall mean down, or a genuine difference in the weather data period (2015-2020 actual precipitation)?
clarification_needed.reason: If the imputation significantly under-represents actual 2010-2014 precipitation, the feature may confuse tree-based models that split on raw precipitation values.
clarification_needed.recommendation: Proceed with current imputation. Investigate discrepancy in Feature Engineering by inspecting the 2015-2020 precipitation mean separately (without imputed rows).
clarification_needed.recommendation_reasoning: The ~2× difference could simply reflect that the month-of-year medians are lower than means (right-skewed precipitation distribution). Non-blocking.
clarification_needed.impact_if_wrong: Moderate — if 2010-2014 precipitation is systematically misrepresented, weather feature importance may be underestimated for the pre-2015 period.

handoff.read_this_first: The CV split uses 3 rolling-origin folds where fold 3 (the PRIMARY split, column _split) is the only fold with post-regime data in training (30 rows, June 2020); h=90 has only 5 scoreable validation rows in fold 3 — Training MUST use all 3 folds for h=90 model selection, not fold 3 alone.

processed_dataset_path.why: Base dataset for all downstream Feature Engineering and Training calls

split_column.why: Primary split assignment based on fold 3; values: train/gap/validation

fold_columns.why: Rolling-origin CV design; Training uses these to implement the 3-fold CV evaluation

split_info_fold3.why: Every downstream metric comparison is conditional on this split; must not change

fit_statistics_source.why: All imputation and scaling parameters fit on train rows only to prevent validation leakage

weather_aggregation_rule.value: mean for all numeric columns; max for Maximum_Temperature, Wind_Gust; min for Minimum_Temperature. Do NOT sum — Visual Crossing API repeats daily totals in each hourly row.
weather_aggregation_rule.why: Sum aggregation produces 24× inflated precipitation values (confirmed by cross-run comparison)

competitor_csv_parsing.why: European semicolon-delimited CSV; commas are data separators within fields

durable_rules.rule: The train/validation split (_split column) is fixed as of iteration 003 and must not be changed for the rest of this run. All model selection, feature evaluation, and metric reporting uses this split.
durable_rules.why: Changing the split mid-run invalidates all metric comparisons across iterations. The selection noise band is conditional on this specific partitioning.
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: All metrics from different iterations become incomparable; model selection is invalidated; the CV design's purpose of testing on post-regime data is defeated

durable_rules.rule: Fit all imputation statistics, scalers, and encoding maps on _split=='train' rows only. Apply (transform) to all rows.
durable_rules.why: Standard leakage prevention. Validation rows must not influence what 'normal' looks like.
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: Validation metrics are optimistically biased; model selection favors models that 'remembered' the validation period

durable_rules.rule: For h=90 model selection, Training must use all 3 CV folds (_fold_1, _fold_2, _fold_3), NOT fold 3 alone.
durable_rules.why: Fold 3 has only 5 scoreable h=90 val rows. MAE estimate from 5 rows has very high variance. Any apparent winner at h=90 from fold 3 alone is likely noise.
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: h=90 champion selection is driven by noise, not genuine performance; holdout h=90 error will be much worse than expected

durable_rules.rule: wx_Precipitation is in mm/day (daily total, mean of 24 identical hourly records). Do NOT re-aggregate from raw parquet — use the preprocess CSV values directly.
durable_rules.why: Visual Crossing API stores daily total repeated in each hourly row; summing gives 24× inflated values
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: If raw parquet is re-aggregated with sum, precipitation features will be 24× inflated, making is_heavy_rain threshold meaningless and any precipitation coefficient nonsensical

durable_rules.rule: Competitor columns (comp_*) outside coverage window (pre-2017-07-01, post-2020-09-15) are filled with 0 — this is the correct structural value, NOT imputation. Always use comp_data_available indicator alongside comp_n_competitors_closed.
durable_rules.why: VerlofConcurrent.csv records events. Absence of a record = no event occurred = 0. A model that treats 0 as 'unknown' will confuse the absence of competitor holidays with competitor holidays occurring on 0 days.
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: If 0s are imputed with competitor mean (~0.73), the model sees phantom competitor closures across 2010-2016, potentially creating a spurious positive correlation

durable_rules.rule: had_reduction is near-constant (99.9% = 1). Feature Engineering must drop it.
durable_rules.why: Zero-variance feature; cannot predict anything; adds noise to model training
durable_rules.cost_if_broken: Minor — tree models will auto-ignore it; linear models waste a coefficient; negligible MAE impact

methodological_cautions.caution: Fold 3 training contains only 30 post-regime rows (June 2020). The model has approximately 4-5 Monday observations as training signal for the regime_x_monday interaction. This is minimal and should not be treated as sufficient to reliably estimate Monday demand.
methodological_cautions.why: The regime change is 2020-06-01; fold 3 training ends 2020-06-30. There are at most 4-5 Mondays in June 2020.
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: If the model's Monday coefficient is calibrated on 4-5 observations, it will be noisy. Diagnosis must check Monday prediction error specifically. Feature Engineering should use domain-knowledge priors for Monday demand level (see domain research: Monday demand is lower than other weekdays because Monday bread-buying is not culturally established).

methodological_cautions.caution: h=90 has only 5 scoreable fold 3 validation rows. Any h=90 validation metric reported from fold 3 alone should be disregarded. Use pooled 3-fold metrics for h=90.
methodological_cautions.why: 5 rows is insufficient for a reliable MAE estimate. Standard error of MAE with n=5 is ~45% of the mean MAE.
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: Selecting a h=90 champion based on fold 3 alone is equivalent to random model selection at that horizon.

methodological_cautions.caution: Weather imputation for pre-2015 rows (1015 rows, 35% of training) uses month-of-year medians from 2015-2020. Belgium precipitation is right-skewed (medians < means), so median imputation understates historical rainfall for 2010-2014 rows. This may suppress weather feature importance in the pre-2015 period.
methodological_cautions.why: Right-skewed distribution means median < mean; imputing with median understates the central tendency for non-rainy-day precipitation.
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: Weather features may appear less important in training (35% of rows have understated precipitation) than they would be if actual 2010-2014 weather data were available. A model tuned on this data may underweight precipitation features.

methodological_cautions.caution: The competitor closure data has a structural confound: the days with the most competitor closures (official public holidays) are also the days Aernoudt may be closed (zero bread_quantity). A naive correlation between comp_n_competitors_closed and bread_quantity will be downward-biased.
methodological_cautions.why: On public holidays, n_competitors_closed is high AND Aernoudt demand may be zero. The genuine positive demand-redirection effect (August summer vacations) is masked by the holiday confound in raw correlation.
methodological_cautions.cost_if_ignored: Feature Engineering may drop or penalise the competitor feature based on low observed correlation, when the true effect (August summer vacation period) is genuine but hidden by the holiday confound.
